title: Bounded derived objects with essentially small cohomology
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with a chosen ordinary derived category $D(\mathcal A)$, and let $w$ be a universe. Suppose $D(\mathcal A)$ has $w$-small Hom sets. Let $P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of objects of $\mathcal A$ admitting a $w$-small family of representatives. Then the property of bounded objects $K$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ such that $P(H^nK)$ for every integer $n$ admits a $w$-small family of representatives. No closure of $P$ under extensions, nor a zero-object hypothesis on $P$, is required. This uses the size convention of [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: All shifts of degree-zero objects from a small family form a small family of single-cohomology objects. By induction, fixed finite iterated extensions of this family remain essentially small, using small Hom sets to bound connecting morphisms.

For an object bounded in [a,a+d], split off top cohomology via the truncation triangle and induct on d. The case d=0 is the single-cohomology isomorphism. Isomorphism invariance transports P along these comparisons. Therefore every bounded object belongs to some finite iterated-extension family. The union over d in the natural numbers is a small family. This is the complete existing source proof, including the possibly empty class P.
